help.title: Help
help.metaDescription: Learn how to use Code Printer. Guides on features like page breaks, margin controls, find and replace, and more.

about.title: About This Service
about.p1: Code Printer is a web application designed to help developers print or convert source code into clean, well-formatted PDF documents.
about.p2: It offers various features such as syntax highlighting, page breaking, real-time preview, and powerful editing tools to optimize your code output experience.

editor.title: Code Editor
editor.p1: You can paste or write your source code here. The code will be automatically syntax-highlighted.

preview.title: Live Preview
preview.p1: The code entered in the editor is displayed in real-time as it will be printed. Adjust various options like font, size, and margins to create your desired output.

pageBreak.title: Page Break
pageBreak.p1: The red dotted line on the preview screen indicates the automatic page break position based on A4 paper.
pageBreak.p2: Clicking the 'Add Page Break' button inserts a manual page break marker (%%%%%%%%%% PAGE_BREAK %%%%%%%%%%) at the cursor's position in the code editor. This marker appears as a blue line in the preview and will also break the page in the actual print.

margins.title: Page Margins
margins.p1: Left and right margins are fixed at 15mm. Top and bottom margins can be adjusted directly in the preview. The adjusted margins are also reflected in the calculation of the red automatic page break lines.

findReplace.title: Find and Replace
findReplace.p1:
You can find specific text or replace it with other text using the Find/Replace feature. It also supports search and replace including newline characters (
).

quickClean.title: Quick Clean
quickClean.p1: Perform common code cleaning tasks with a single click. (e.g., removing consecutive empty lines, lifting closing brackets)

undoRedo.title: Undo / Redo
undoRedo.p1: You can undo (Ctrl+Z) or redo (Ctrl+Y) up to the last 50 actions.

post1.title: 5 Tips for Clean Code Output
post1.p1: When converting source code to PDF or printing it, readability is crucial. Whether it's for a code review with colleagues, a school assignment, or personal archiving, well-organized code is easier to understand and looks more professional. Here are five tips to improve your code output quality with our Code Printer.
post1.p2: It is recommended to use a monospaced font designed for coding. Fonts like D2Coding, Fira Code, and Consolas ensure that characters occupy the same width, maintaining perfect code alignment. They also clearly distinguish between the number '0' and the letter 'O', and the number '1' and the letter 'l', reducing potential confusion.
post1.p3: Syntax highlighting is a great help in visually grasping the structure of your code. When variables, functions, and reserved words are displayed in different colors, you can follow the flow of the code quickly. Our Code Printer supports syntax highlighting for various programming languages, so it's automatically applied when you paste your code.
post1.p4: Proper margins are a key design element that makes content comfortable to view. Setting sufficient margins around your code block eliminates a cramped feeling and improves readability. Adjust the top, bottom, left, and right margins in the print settings to find the optimal layout.
post1.p5: You wouldn’t want an important function or class to be cut off in the middle of a page. With our service's 'PAGE_BREAK' feature, you can manually break the page wherever you want. This allows you to group code into logical units, enhancing the completeness of the output.
post1.p6: Before printing, it’s a good idea to clean up things like `console.log` statements for debugging or unused comments. Keep only the most essential and important code in the final output to create a clean and tidy result.
post1.p7: Use these tips to make your source code shine! Our Code Printer will always be there to help you create the best possible output.
